title: A Morning Under Sail on the Astrea
coverImageAlt: Placeholder — real photo of the Astrea under sail to come
excerpt: Most mornings in the bay are glassy until midday. This one wasn't.
subtitle: Good Medicine's sister boat, running close-hauled out of Marina de La Paz on a rare morning with wind before nine.
author: Flavia Ibarra
body:
Wind before nine is unusual enough in the bay that the crew mentioned it twice before we'd even left the marina. We had the sails up by 8:15 and were close-hauled past the breakwater by 8:30.

The Astrea handles better upwind than her size suggests, which is the sort of thing you only really notice once you're the one on the helm trying to hold a line through a gust.

> Most days here are about patience. This one was just about sailing.

![Boat placeholder — real photo of the Astrea at anchor to come](/assets/img/boat-baydreamer-exterior.webp "The Astrea at anchor later that afternoon, wind gone as predicted.")

By eleven the wind had died back to the usual afternoon calm, right on schedule. We motored the last stretch back, which is how most days here actually end.

It's not the kind of morning you can plan for. You just have to be on the water often enough that you're there when it happens.
